mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market and economic expansion, which should drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the Rank IC between UNRATE and SPX returns is less than 0.05 over a 5-year window, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is growing, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are negative in more than 30% of cases when UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which should positively impact related sectors and drive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases when HOUST growth > 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rates reduce corporate profitability and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in more than 30% of cases during a monetary tightening cycle, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production growth (INDPRO) indicates increased economic activity and supply, which should drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the Rank IC between INDPRO and SPX returns is less than 0.03 over a 5-year window, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) show growth, it indicates strong aggregate demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 0.5% quarter-over-quarter and RSAFS growth > 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: If SPX returns are negative in more than 30% of cases when GDPC1 and RSAFS both show growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases when PAYEMS growth > 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.
